who are devoid of pure conduct and averse to the Kaula way—
One should always avoid water offered according to the Vedas or by the Vaiṣṇavas;
one should also avoid the offering of funeral cakes, the shedding of tears, and the state of being a bound soul (paśubhāva).
One should instead contemplate the eternally risen, most powerful Self through the nature of the Self.
The Great Reality, eternally arisen, abides in the state of self-awareness.
All those who possess contraction [of consciousness] should consume [the offerings] like death itself;
one should strive by every means for the sake of the cause, which is the food of the heroes.
Endowed with compassion and courtesy, yet unattached to heroic deeds;
devoted to yoga as a yoginī, detached from the teachings for the bound (paśu);
these fortunate ones are called great heroes (mahāvīra), delighting in the assembly of yogins (yogimelāpaka).
Having thus recognized the practitioner and having revealed this sequence,
the preceptor— endowed with heroism, free from greed, and devoid of hypocrisy—
[should provide] light drinks and light food for one who has reached the further shore of knowledge and realization.
Free from idle chatter, envy, fear, and dejection,
it is characterized by the essential marks of the movements and conduct of the Yoginīs.
One should observe all the signs of death or untimely death.
[This is] the fourth, which delights in the Krama and is adorned by the Krama;
it is the Yoga that delights in the oral tradition (mukhāgama), protected by the Yoginīs, and guarded by Yoga.
One should sequentially observe the body through the application of the yoga of vision (*dṛṣṭiyoga*).
O Dear One, the emergence of Kuṇḍalinī from the center of the *kanda* is known.
Within the centers of the lotuses of the navel and the heart, one should draw up the form of nectar.
The movement of the eyes occurs at the heart-lotus and the throat-pit;
by the abandonment of the earth-element at the uvula, the bindu, and the space between the eyebrows, there arises the movement into the sky.
This occurs in the Brahma-aperture, which is always unobstructed, for a distance of twelve finger-breadths.
As long as one encounters a path, one performs coming and going;
having lost all shadow through practice, one should gaze with the vision of Brahman,
O beautiful one, entering into all beings like the sun into water.
Because through such practice, even one who is unfit may attain fitness;
though devoid of all auspicious marks and lacking in all scriptural knowledge,
he shall become Bhairava himself, his body being known as Saṃkarṇya.
The ritual preparations, the necessary materials, and the authorized person are found in the family tradition (*kulāgama*).
One whose intellect is well-guarded should not reveal this, along with its defining characteristics, to anyone.
Then, the lineage teacher (*kulācārya*) or a worthy person born from a portion of that [teacher]—one who is slender-waisted [and pure]—[should perform the rite].
Otherwise, they would not be revealed even in hundreds of lifetimes.
Thus, O Bhairavī, it has been told by me according to the capacity [of the disciple].
The Śrī Devī said:
By your grace, O Bhairava, I have heard the characteristics of those who accomplish heroic feats, for whom this narration must be performed; tell me that rite.
That [mantra] of seventeen syllables which is dear to the Dwellers of the Sacred Seats—[tell me of it].
(122a) Regarding the sixty-four and eight seats, tell me the mantra-word of that mistress of the central seat, who is the leader of the sequence of the four.
O Mahādeva, tell me that mantra which has no equal among tens of millions, hundreds of thousands, and tens of thousands of mantras; I have never heard it before.
Śrī Bhairava said:

O Dear One, this [teaching] regarding the four sequential worship rituals, together with its secret, is known as the "Fourfold Kālikā"; it has been designated by means of the mantra. Since there is no further distinction between them, I have revealed this out of affection for you.
This is that supreme Goddess, who spreads forth into infinite divisions.
Having extracted [the essence] from these divisions and assumed a thirteenth form,
she exists through her distinct names as the creepers of the *Āvalī* in their proper sequence.
By merely worshipping it once, one attains identity with that [deity].
I shall describe that power which partakes in enjoyment;
[it should be established] on a level, pure, and beautiful patch of ground, well-concealed by a wise man.
In that auspicious place, smeared with honey and wine, sprinkled with saffron,
rich with the fragrance of musk and sandalwood, gladdened by the scent of camphor,
most delightful, strewn with flowers, and thick with large blossoms.
It should be covered with red flowers, or by the Self-Existent One himself;
or with various colorful powders of the earth, such as turuṣka, aguru, and sihlaka;
or else with the finest guggulu resin mixed with clarified butter.
Having well-incensed with those incenses, one should then extract the mantra.
There, O Gaṇāmbikā, one should worship the Mātṛkā, the mother of mantras,
joined with the eight groups of consonants and brilliantly illuminated by a garland of lamps.
Having performed that worship of the wheel, one should then extract the Vidyā.
Then, standing at night, firm and composed, or established in power, one who is steadfast in his vows [should proceed].
One should cause to be offered various kinds of food— solid foods, soft foods, things to be licked, and things to be sucked—
as well as fish and roasted meats, both raw and cooked. All large-bodied creatures and those born from the atmosphere should also be presented.
One should cause to be served well-prepared cooked foods that are suitable for drinking;
they should have the color of molten red iron, be most beautiful in their middle portion,
possess the taste of supreme bliss, and be as formidable as a rolling mass [of energy].
One should contemplate the wine as resembling a ruby, the supreme bliss and nectar, fragrant; where it is, one should offer it with effort.
O auspicious lady, all of those [substances] should be combined with *surā* and *sīdhu*.
They should be joined with worthy heroes and united in the mind with mantras;
they must be avoided by those devoid of mantras, for thereby there would be a loss of accomplishment (*siddhi*).
Those who move upon the earth, as well as those who move in the directions and so forth, seek out any flaw.
Therefore, one should avoid her with effort and remember the previously mentioned characteristics.
As for the mutual discourse of the *cakra*, the mutual conversation in the assembly of heroes (*vīragoṣṭhī*),
those [women] who reside in the seats (*pīṭha*) within the *cakra*, as well as the masters of practitioners (*sādhakeśvara*), [should be honored].
But the mutual sacrifice, free from impurity and most beautiful—
thus [it is stated] in the *Jayadrathayāmala*, in the *Kālikula*.
Śrī Bhairava said:

First, O Dear One, one should remember the messenger (dūtī), both externally and internally, along with her various garments and those endowed with devotion to the Mother. The messenger must be employed in every respect; one who is devoid of the messenger does not attain success.
Thus, according to the procedure stated in the Cakra, listen now to its majesty:
having rescued twenty-one million and eight hundred members of one's lineage,
they go to the world of Rudra for as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.
(123a) If this [attainment] should occur for those of purified soul according to the method taught in the Cakra,
there would be a fall from that lineage due to association with those of no noble family.

O Goddess praised by heroes, if one desires one's own welfare, success, a very long life, or union with the Yoginīs, one must never perform [the ritual] in a single vessel within the family tradition (*kulāmnāya*).
Meditation destroys those bonds of the past and future.
One must carefully avoid eating with them, as well as drinking and socializing;
one should avoid even speaking with them, O beloved, let alone physical touch.

Upon touching a person who has not been initiated, one should perform the purificatory bath associated with fire (āgneyasnāna). Furthermore, if through delusion one should ever come into contact with saliva or similar impurities arising from such contact, it must be accompanied by not seeing [the person] again and abstaining from eating together with them.

He undergoes expiation and performs the worship of the sacrifice again. Endowed with the stages of initiation and so forth, he is a reciter of mantras firm in his vows, a possessor of the Kula instruction, and purified by all the sacraments.
There is no accomplishment through contact with the bound (paśu), nor from the disparagement of the Vision (darśana). One attains dullness of intellect, or else the mantra fails;
for this reason, O blessed lady, the lineage of the bound must be avoided.
The Śrī Devī said:
You have stated that one should diligently avoid the state of being a *paśu* (bound soul);
indeed, the essential nature of the state of being a *pati* (lord) was previously explained by you.
"What kind of distinction has been proclaimed? Being deluded, she does not understand at all.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"Now I shall explain another [method], provided that it is not otherwise accomplished."
O Beloved, that heroic latent impression (*vāsanā*) must be guarded with great effort;
by the mere recognition of its characteristic, one becomes a sky-farer (*khecarī*).
The *golaka* is quickly produced, and his state as a bound animal (*paśu*) perishes.
Aṭṭahāsa is at the site of the crest-lock, and Caritra is at the cavity of the hand;
Kullagiri is on the ear, O beloved, and Jayantī is in the northern course.
O Dear One, Ujjayinī is at the center of the eyebrows; Prayāga is situated in the middle of the face; Vārāṇasī is in the heart; the Śrīpīṭha is on both shoulders;
Viraja is in the region of the throat; and Heruṇḍa is in the belly.
O Dear One, Alaṃpura is in the middle of the navel; Saṃdor and Ūrdhvalāpura are there as well. Gokarṇa is at the base of the *kanda*, while Maruddeśa is within the *bhaga*.
Furthermore, Paribhadra is to be known by the practitioner as being in the penis.
Saktinagara is on the right [arm], Pauṇḍravardhana on the left;
Purastīra is on the left shoulder, while Pṛṣṭhāpura is on the right.
Udyākeśī is between the knees, and Sopāra is said to be in the space between them.

Kṣīrikā is in the left hand, and Māyāpurī is in the right. Āmrātakeśvara is at the left ankle, and the auspicious Rājagṛha is at the [right] ankle. At the base of the feet are Brahmāṇī and Kālāgnividyārakī.
Thus, O auspicious lady, one who desires their own welfare should constantly remember this latent impression (*vāsanā*) within the heart;
women are to be honored for the sake of their own spiritual accomplishment. And having thus understood the impelling force, she is the cutter-in-the-middle (*madhye hyālakṛntanī*).
The power of the Supreme Lord, whose form resembles a thread of wool, is Śakti;
that which resides at the very end of her is known as Saṃkarṣaṇī,
within whom the interval of the six seasons proceeds in a state of internal dissolution.
At that time, she indeed swallows it, being devoid of both dissolution and emergence.
O Dear One, that movement of the *prāṇa* and *apāna* which has neither emergence nor dissolution is where one finds rest;
there, twenty-one thousand [breaths] come to rest.
At that time, she indeed devours him as he travels along the path of the three channels;
having entered within him, she is of the nature of light and consists of mind.

That pure constituent of his nature is another aspect, whose form is space. O Beloved, by you— who reside within the wave, who flow as the movement of prāṇa and apāna, and whose own form and body are space— his [nature] has been destroyed.
Having ignited the fire of time, she who pierces the foundation of the wheel awakens;
residing in the abode of the *kanda*, she remains in the form of a serpent.
Situated within the moon and the sun, she is celebrated as the fire [of consciousness] with the jewels upon her hoods.
Established in the form of a thread, it ascends the upper path;
flowing through the midst of the chain, it alone is the divider of the three.
Resembling a lotus fiber, it flows from the heart to the palate.

O Goddess, having seized the mind at the end of the twelve [petals], she enters her own city like nectar resembling milk, nourishing the individual soul (jīva). Having paid homage to her, who is the sovereign of all the wheels (cakras), [one honors] the mistress of them all.

Now hear from me the mantras of that God beyond gods. O Dear One, regarding the previously mentioned site and the previously mentioned practitioners: first, one must choose a teacher who is endowed with a female messenger, has conquered his senses, and possesses the qualities already described.
Then one should extract the mantras; by means of those not seen by others, one shall attain liberation.
Listen with a single-minded focus, O auspicious lady, for I shall extract them according to reality:
one should join Mohanī, Kālamālā, and Vīranātha.
The first mantra, possessed of a fierce [syllable] that has seized the vital breath and accompanied by the staff (*daṇḍa*);
joined with the ninth [vowel], it is Gaṇeśa joined with the seventh [consonant].
(The first) fourth [vowel] mounted upon the sixth [consonant], and *ṭā-ṭi-bhaṃ* joined with the third [vowel].
The face of the well is Mahākāla, adorned with the fourth vowel;
mounted upon Tejas is Gāṇḍīva,
and immediately after that, Gāṇḍīva— resplendent with the darkness of frost— is joined with arrows.
One should extract [the mantra] consisting of five streams, which includes Vaiṣṇava and Kāmadeva, seated upon the seat of Citrabhānu, and endowed with my ornaments. (124b)
This eighteen-syllable vidyā is remembered as most terrible and even more terrible than the terrible.
By the mere remembrance of it, a man becomes the lord of the universe;
he creates everything in its entirety and withdraws it all with ease.
O Goddess, from this [source] have emerged numerous vidyās;
here there are various kramas and innumerable kulas,
as well as many lineages of oral tradition and manifold gharayajñas.
There is nothing she does not know; there is nothing that is not accomplished through her.
There is nothing not pervaded by her; there is nothing she would not withdraw.
There is no yoga whatsoever that has not emerged from the Goddess.
This sport belongs to the Supreme Goddess, known as Kālasaṃkarṣaṇī;
it consists of various arrangements of objects born of manifold forms and transformations,
strewn with diverse clusters of jewels, and containing various other worlds.
Mahāmāyā has emerged from that Goddess of goddesses, who dwells within all things as numerous as tens of millions of cosmic eggs; by her,
this entire universe is pervaded, and the creation of the worlds occurs again and again.
Therefore, they will speak of that state which is supreme and auspicious;
it has been described to you, O lady of good vows, merely in brief and by way of indication.
Listen further, O beautiful one, as I tell you the truth according to its meaning.
One should meditate upon the syllable *lakṣmī* (*hrīṃ*), which is free from agitation and endowed with splendor.
It is taught that the two *kulapiṇḍas* are surmounted by the head-syllable (*haṃ*) and splendor (*tejas*).
This mantra, which increases all prosperity, is to be employed in all *cakras*.
The trees belonging to the families of the Kṣetrapālas are joined with their respective names as weapons;
they are worshipped according to the sequence of the Mantrapīṭha, beginning with the feet,
O Dear One, in the directions of the East, South, West, and North.
(125a) A group of six should be formed there according to the sequence of worship.
O Dear One, those Yoginīs born of the sacred fields who are the wish-fulfilling trees of the cremation grounds—
She should be worshipped with white flowers and divine, delightful incenses.
One should cause twenty-four lamps to be offered in every direction.
[The vessel] is broad at the back and base, and rounded in the middle.

Measuring eight finger-breadths in height and four finger-breadths in width, it should be fashioned with equal proportions from top to bottom. Once completed, it should be joined with a lamp and placed upon a red wick.
One should dismiss the water-pot, the blindfolds, and the mandalas;

without these, there can be no accomplishment. O Mother of the Gaṇas, [one should also dismiss] the fire, the *śruva* ladle, and so forth, along with the vessels previously mentioned that are filled with wine.

In the center, the slender-waisted goddess is to be worshipped according to the method described for the elixir (rasāyana). O lady of beautiful hips, the Mistress of the Seat (pīṭhanāyakī) is indeed to be worshipped in the four directions with wine and liquor, O auspicious one who shines with the limbs of spirits.
Once the ground has been smeared with the dung of a tawny cow, one should not smear it again in the center.
Thus ends the determination of worship in the *Jayadrathayāmala*, within the *Kālikākula*.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Having prepared two vessels for the *argha* offering, or even just one,
and having looked upon them with the Power (*śakti*), endowed with the Supreme Reality (*paratattva*),
one who is joined with the contemplation of that state should always cultivate pure consciousness (*saṃvitti*).
One should cause the arghya vessel to be taken; it should be made of silver or gold. Alternatively, an excellent earthen vessel, free from cracks or flaws, is best;
one should take an excellent vessel made from a root that grows out of season and then begin the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).
Whether in the forenoon or the afternoon, or indeed throughout the day and night,
one should recite the Pīṭhastotra; at night, one should perform the recitation with a concentrated mind.
When the clear dawn has arrived, one should perform the *vīrabhojya* (hero’s feast).
Through this, the dawning of great fortune occurs; one may attain a kingdom or become a sky-walker (*khecara*).
Even if one is of dull intellect, the hero attains perfection through this consumption.
Having seen disease, famine, death, thieves, fire, and robbers; the terrible fear of foreign armies, untimely death, and various other such calamities, the number of which is not known—
O Goddess, one should constantly destroy whatever [obstacles] exist through those whose powers are unfailing. Here, one should feed a virgin and yogins who are equal to the end of the heroes.
Thousands of sins of killing a Brahmin and hundreds of expiations [are thereby removed].
By performing worship even once, one becomes the recipient of ten million worships.
The Yoginīs reside in the cremation ground, at the wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣa), and in the sacred field (kṣetra).
For the purpose of malevolent rites (abhicāra), one should go to the cremation ground; however, at the wish-fulfilling tree, success (siddhi) is granted.
The Yoginīs are present at the gathering of the sacred fields (*kṣetramelāpa*) according to the *Sarvasiddhikulāgama*.
The Śrī Devī said:
"O Lord of Gods, what else is there in the *Kulāgama*? Tell me, O Master."

O Mahādeva, you have indeed spoken concerning this Kula-mādhava; however, there is something else that deserves special attention by your grace—please deign to tell it to me. Describe what kind of cremation ground is proclaimed, and speak to me of the Kalpa-tree.
"Tell me of the field of the Yoginīs, which is the favor toward others found nowhere else.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"The cremation ground is the region of the heart, and the wish-fulfilling tree is Kuṇḍalī."
The Yoginīs are to be known as being in the field between the eyebrows within the family of Yoginīs.
Such, O Great Goddess, is the worship of the Kula here, O Beloved;
it is accomplished instantly, O Goddess, if there is the oral tradition (mukhāgama).
The Śrī Devī said:
(126a) O God, do not conceal this; that which is devoid of the Krama does not attain success.
All fragmentary knowledge is but a fragmented wheel; it does not partake in liberation.
O Lord, do not disregard me; one should not conceal one's entire essence.
If you have affection for me, then truly reveal your own nature.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Where there is expansion, there is contraction; therein lies the supreme nectar.
Resembling the fiber of a lotus stalk, it is the grasper of both knowledge and realized wisdom.
Moving as the mistress of all wheels (*sarvacakreśī*), she resides in the wheel and dwells in the center.
Free from qualities and free from conceptual construction, she is the sustainer of the foundation of the worlds.
She is fivefold and threefold, bestowing the reality of the Kula.
Having entered that state through the practice, those lords of Akula abide in that station.
By means of the union of mind and consciousness within the seventeen-syllable mantra,
one restrains the two pulsations (spandas) that are devoid of both dissolution and emergence.
The material body is abandoned through the realization "I am [the Self]" alone, and not otherwise.
O Beloved, all those former and future karmas— manifesting as obstacles and produced by the unimpaired power of *prakṛti*— forcibly delude you.
The mind does not delight in those; one should settle the mind in the middle.
"I do not exist, nor does another exist," [one should think] in the state of absolute peace.
If one can cultivate this innate state for even a moment, one finds rest therein.
Then, having become a sky-farer (khecara), he shall attend a gathering of yoginīs.
Having performed meditation in their midst, he should enter the many [yoginīs] born of his own body.
The wheel of twenty-four [deities], crowded together, is beheld by her.
That meditation which is within my midst has indeed been declared in the Mukhāgama.
Therefore, O auspicious lady, the sequence of worship is otherwise; it is the meditation of the bound soul (paśu).
By this practice, the sequence is worshipped; otherwise, one is a bound soul.
Whosoever is a worshiper empowered by that state, a worshiper of the Krama,
otherwise would be a mere prattler, excluded from mantra and tantra. (126b)
Listen with a single-minded focus, O beloved, for I shall now describe the second path:
wherever there is a famous cremation ground, whether in a village or even in a city,
those people who have reached old age and those individuals who meditate there—
At the edge of a village, in the middle of a village, at a solitary tree, or in a secluded place;
or in the house of a courtesan, or in a gathering—this is to be known as the house of the Yoginīs.
O Goddess, it must always be kept secret; this is what the practitioner must know.
The cremation ground is well-established within the center of the house, situated at the entrance of the mouth;
having known this through the realization of Brahman, it is indeed the lineage of the Guru.
O Goddess of the Field of the Yoginīs, the junction (*sandhi*) is indeed present in all accomplishments.
O auspicious one, the wish-fulfilling tree stands in the center as the support and sustainer;
here is established the assembly of the entire host of yoginīs.
He who knows this is a knower of reality and becomes a follower of the Kula tradition.

Thus, he who indeed does not know the threefold worship of the sacred sites (sthānapūjana) is a beast from birth to birth; he wanders through many bodies born of his own karma. First, one should practice the internal yoga (ādhyātmika-yoga), which is like a meal that is neither bitter nor insipid, but well-prepared.
If one performs worship even once by means of the practice of self-awareness,
one shall dwell in the midst of the sky-farers (khecaras), joined with tens of millions of *kulakoṭis*;
such a person is the doer of all, the enjoyer of all, and the creator, the Lord of the World.
How do those who know reality understand external worship?
The Śrī Devī said:
"I have heard everything without exception, yet I am desirous of further inquiry."
And how do those others who are devoted to other systems of philosophy achieve success on this earth?
Those who are devoid of this path, who do not know the secret tradition (guptāmnāya),
whose mantras lack potency, and whose practitioners possess deluded intellects— [how can they succeed]?
For those who lack the gathering [of practitioners] and are devoid of the purpose of storing provisions,
how can there be accomplishment for them? Tell me, especially, what else could it be?
The illustrious Bhairava said:
"To whichever person one belongs through the application of mantras and who stands firm in the stage of tantric conduct,
I shall explain that for him so that it is accomplished according to reality."
O Dear One, one should begin the sacrifice by means of this sequential method;
one should worship one’s own lineage in the center and avoid the practice of duality.
The Goddess said:
"How is the practice of duality (dvaitācāra) described, and what is non-duality (advaita) like, O Lord? By knowing which one may become free from doubt and never again fall into delusion?
Śrī Bhairava said:
Those who follow the left and right tantras, whether they belong to the non-families (akula) or the families (kula),
are declared in the Sauragāruḍa to have arisen from the substance of non-duality.
Those who drink wine and other intoxicants, wearing garlands and well-adorned by the drinking of liquor—
Those who are endowed with the practice of non-duality (*advaitācāra*) and are remembered as being dual in substance (*dravyadvaita*),
whose mantras and conceptualizations consist of aggregates of measures (*mātrā*),
and who have attained complete perfection through the Śākta [path]— they are to be worshipped in the center of the wheel (*cakramadhya*).
The Vaiṣṇava, Buddhist, and Vedic doctrines are indeed [diverse] views;
they should be avoided with great effort, for they are remembered as being like cattle.
Indeed, due to contact with non-dual substances, they abandon their proximity [to the truth].
They turn away from the goal; they are lifeless and devoid of the vital principle.
Indeed, there is no worship for them, as they lack strength and are bereft of the proper sequence. Those who are devoid of the signs of realization do not partake in the fruit of accomplishment.

Those who are devoid of austerity and recitation, who are bereft of worship and fire-offerings, and who have fallen into the notion that they are the mantra itself— those mantras have reached the state of being bound souls (paśu).
Indeed, they are destitute of their own power, lacking radiance and deprived of divine presence.
And through his grace, the practitioners of Śakti achieve success in the worship and discourse of the *cakra*;
consequently, they become bestowers of fruits, granting the attainment of liberation, desire, and wealth.
It must not be given to just anyone; having given it to such a person, no spiritual accomplishment (siddhi) is seen.

It should be worshipped according to the tradition (āmnāya) by those who delight in the Kula scriptures. However, those who are devoid of the tantric conduct (tantrācāra) must be avoided with great effort.
Thus ends "The Determination of Tantric Conduct" from the *Jayadrathayāmala*, within the *Kālikula*.
The venerable Goddess said:
"You have proclaimed the root mantra and the procedure for the non-dual sacrifice."
O Supreme Lord, tell me that without which no accomplishment whatsoever may occur; O Lord of Gods, explain to me the supreme determination of substances,
without which neither knowledge nor the eternal tradition can exist.
What are the substances of the *vakula* [family], and what is the family drink?
What is their food, and what should be their mode of conduct? What is the worship in the *kula* paths for those who abide in the practice of non-duality?
Śrī Bhairava said:
This secret spoken by Bhairava is not to be disclosed;
it must be guarded with great effort so that the world does not censure it.
Onion, garlic, and the like, *laṃbu*, *śal*, and *tarkaśā*,
as well as other parts of these, along with flowers—
O fortunate one, these substances are recommended in the Kula path.
O Goddess, auspicious water, divine liquor, blood, wine, great oil, and *sīdhuka*;
that which arises from the *kuṇḍa* and *goḷa*—these, O Goddess, are the drinks born of the *kula*.
[Likewise] fish and meat arising from the great ocean, and those of creatures dwelling on land or moving through the sky.
But the one who is free from conceptual construction always provides food for all:
whether she be a mother, a sister, a wife, a daughter, or a female relative;
whether she be Mātaṅgī, Kajjalī, Śauṇḍī, Kaṇdukī, or Carmaraṅginī.
Dhvajinī, Asthivijalī, Dhīvarī, and Cakriṇī, O beloved;
these indeed are the great seats (*mahāpīṭha*) from which noble women have arisen.
One who desires one's own success should always conduct oneself with them;

that is, with those who are appointed by others as the supreme among all classes of *indrajāla* practitioners, and with the female messengers (*dūtīs*) who are joined with the reality of those engaged in the ritual feast (*bhojana*). One should be united with them.
Thus, through the application of saṃsāra, worship is indeed considered superior.
But then, worship should be performed by means of conduct free from hesitation.
Then, O Goddess, he attains success, provided that what has been enjoyed by them has been meditated upon.
It is known as that which, through drinking, touching, and eating, severs the bonds.
That beautiful practice of non-duality (advaitācāra), which was previously concealed by me,
belongs to those who are endowed with the Kaula instructions and who delight in the ancient tradition.
Those animals are purifiers, and purifiers are remembered as animals;
by this application of food, one who acts without knowing goes to hell.
Those who have attained the state of knowledge go rightly to the midst of the sky.
This has been revealed for the sake of sacrifice for the benefit of the foremost of practitioners.
Those who are devoid of that power shall not attain accomplishment;
therefore, with every effort, one should perform the sacrifice together with her.
If one performs the sacrifice otherwise, everything of his perishes.
[It should be performed] in a well-concealed, solitary, and delightful hero-field (vīrakṣetra) for the sake of attainments (siddhi).
[The practitioners] are naked, free from shame, and worshipers of the non-dual lineage.
The body should worship one another through the enjoyment of food, drink, and so forth;
likewise, the two lovers, joined with those born of the *kuṇḍa* and *gola* lineages,
together with the *māna* and *maṇḍaka*, should enjoy one another.
To be joined from mouth to mouth, there is food, drink, and kissing—
green, variegated, diverse, and auspicious—
just as the thunderbolt is in Indra’s hand and the water-pot in Brahmā’s.
Just as the trident and the discus are in my hand, and as they are in Hari’s,
so too, O heroes, are the mistress of yoga and the purifiers such as garlic [in yours].
Onions, garlic, and other substances prescribed for use—
those considered purifying, auspicious, and conducive to prosperity— are traditionally held to protect sacrifices;
they are free from obstacles, capable of neutralizing impediments, and are pure, joyful, and auspicious.
Where there is no garlic, there is neither spiritual perfection nor liberation;
elsewhere there is no "hero's feast" (vīrabhojya), nor indeed any sacrifice that bestows success.
It is only there that the ritual of summoning (saṃnidhīkaraṇa) and the assembly (melāpa) take place.

Just as all sacrifices and other rites are fruitless without clarified butter (ājya), so too, O Goddess, O Beloved, [the rites] are fruitless without the jewels of Soma in both the Kula and Akula traditions.
"Soma" is said to be the onion, and especially the garlic.
Others, who were impure and lacking in self-restraint, remained there on that portion of the Himavat mountain;
yet all [the others] are remembered as being entirely pure, beneficial, and sanctified.
O auspicious lady, they remove all diseases and bestow all good fortune;
they bring about the presence of Kulakaula, which grants the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation,
and yields the desired results for pacification, nourishment, and subjugation.

O beloved, you have heard that he is the destroyer of all calamities and dear to all beings; indeed, your nature is like nectar and cannot be pierced by the forest [of obstacles]. For the sake of Vīrasiṃha’s success, through that [practice], there shall be the destruction of [all] decay.
Even one who constantly consumes that which is kept secret within an underground chamber, combined with the essence of mṛgamoda,
shall become imperishable like Śiva;
he becomes the creator and destroyer in this world— such is the secret perfection.
He is eternally dear to Bhairava and to the multitude of Mothers.
One should satisfy the foremost [deities] with both edible and non-edible foods, as is customary in the world.
Having first performed this rite, the secret Kaula doctrine has been declared by me.
By means of each single exertion, having cast off old age and death,
the hero becomes the supreme among all siddhas, possessing divine status and consuming nectar.
One should burn incense again and again at the gathering of the goddesses.
In whatever place the substance may be, there it shall be determined.
O Bhairavī, [the substances are] garlic or onion, along with wine and liquor.
There, the deities sport with fish, meat, and other offerings;

there, all the Mothers—both those who move through the sky and those who move upon the earth—are present for one desiring spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*). It is there that the emergence of *Kulakaula* occurs, where the woman of the *kula* resides.
When the Kula practitioner abides therein, the arising of all accomplishments occurs;
sporting with one another by means of various great substances,
he is completely liberated from all suffering and entirely freed from all sorrow.
He attains liberation from everything and always remains fearless.
What more shall I say regarding the powers of the practitioner?
The Goddess said:
What indeed is the greatness of the Hero, and especially of the ritual substances?
Those who are endowed with the instructions of their lineage and joined with the practice of non-duality—
by your grace, I have never before heard of their power.
Today my birth has become fruitful, as it has been realized through your grace.
But those Vaiṣṇavas and others are everywhere reviled by the Vedāntins;
for what reason do they suffer such misery, and how is it that they are so devoid of fortune?
For this substance, this drink, which is like nectar, nothing on earth— this human birth so difficult to obtain— is rendered fruitless by external things.
It is obtained again only by chance, if some grace should ever be bestowed.
"Having attained this birth which grants authority, all [other births] become useless.
O Lord, how may I dispel this doubt of mine regarding how one should indeed avoid them?
Śrī Bhairava said:
A substance is not prepared by one who is ignorant, nor by one who has not performed the sacrifice according to the sequence;
there is no success for that which is devoid of ritual procedure, and having offered it, one would go to hell.
In the Brāhmaṇa [tradition], it is prescribed according to ritual injunctions during the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice;
in the Vaiṣṇava tradition, the pure essence (rasa) is to be taken from the Siṃhacakra.
Those among these who are devoid of devotion are considered deluded beasts.
They revile the supreme substance, the eye, which has been cast outside by their own desires.
Then, by that very fault, ignorance arises,
persisting again and again for thousands of births.
They wander again and again through repeated actions and rebirths; until, by the descent of power (*śaktipāta*) which abides in supreme non-duality,
how can there be liberation for one who is attached to the substances of qualified non-duality?
Through the meditation on non-duality, he is liberated from the bonds of worldly existence.
Just as the meditation on one among ten million proceeds according to reality,
so too are the attainments of this yoga— though it may be cluttered with mantras and ritual substances— traditionally taught.
In a state of fearless conduct, practitioners sport in the midst [of the assembly].
Oh, how great is the power of the substance (dravya) in drinking, eating, and other such acts!
What can I say to you regarding those joined with women of noble family?
Throughout thousands of millions of births, they have been devoted to austerity and recitation;
they have performed vows and observances here, as well as the *kṛcchra* and *cāndrāyaṇa* penances,
all sacrifices, and all acts of charity, yet none of these have attained stability anywhere.
Whatever fruit has been proclaimed for those who have performed incalculable millions of times,
the knower of the lineage obtains that very fruit by merely tasting it once.
How much more so for one endowed with faith who worships according to the specific sequence!
O Goddess of the gods, this has indeed been declared for the practitioner who is engaged according to the prescribed rite.
Those who are capable in the Kula traditions but have been excluded from these substances [are as follows].
They are designated as cattle; one should not dwell among them.
This is the majesty found in heroes, revealed out of affection for you.
O Queen of Heroes, she who was previously mentioned shall reside in the sacred seat (pīṭha) upon your face.
O Goddess, one should perform sacrifice together with her; in her house is the supreme sacred seat (pīṭha).
O beautiful one, the abode of Mātaṅgī is proclaimed as Prayāga. O Dear One, Kajjalī is known as Vāruṇa, and Śauṇḍī is in the Kaula-house.
Kaṃdukī is Cāṭṭahāsa, Jayantī is Carmacaṅgiṇī;
Caritra is said to be Dhvajinī, and Vidāriṇī resides at Ekāmra.
The ninth seat is Cakriṇī, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.
The Goddess said:
O All-pervading Lord, where indeed is that place renowned, which is difficult even for the gods to attain,
and which serves as the supreme proof for the benefit of the heroes among heroes?

The ninth seat, Cakriṇī, has been described by you as being ninefold. What is said regarding all its seed-syllables, and what is the resulting state of subjugation? O Bhairava, what is the potency and what is this power of the one named Kauṇḍilya?
Śrī Bhairava said:
That which is the ninth, the Cakriṇī, revolves within the center of the universe;
it crushes all seeds, having divided them into two by means of the six flavors.
And that [power] named Kuṇḍalinī, having emerged from the abode of the kanda, arises from the eight seats; she is the giver of success (siddhi) during the nine months.
And whoever is devoid of her, he [cannot attain] success through the assembly (melāpaka).
Then one should perform the *melāpaka* (conjunction) in the assembly of all yoginīs.
O fair-complexioned lady, the confluence of the *iḍā* and *suṣumnā* is Prayāga;
that which is called Varuṇa is between the eyebrows, and likewise, Kaula is at the uvula (*laṃbikā*).
Nāsāgra is at Aṭṭahāsa, while Jayantī is in the cavity of the palate;
Bindūparicaritrā is in the region of the navel of Ekāmra.
Having known Devīkoṭa to be situated within the *kanda*, one should undertake the pilgrimage.
Just as the Kuṇḍalinī power above the *kanda* has indeed deluded the world, all this has been told to you; tell me, O Bhairavī, what else?
Thus, in the *Jayadrathayāmala*, in the *Kālikula*.
Śrī Bhairava said:
That which is the Kuṇḍalinī energy, established in the secret wheel (*guhyacakra*).
O auspicious lady, that place which grants all desires must always be concealed.
Therefore, it is eternally renowned as "Guhyā," more secret than the secret itself.
The nectar arising from that is difficult even for gods and asuras to obtain.
O Beloved, when thousands of births come to an end in the ocean of one’s lineage, and when the latent impressions of saṃsāra have been entirely exhausted,
then for that person whose body is completely purified, contemplation reaches that state.

When grace was bestowed upon him by the high-souled Bhairava, the god beyond gods, then his intellect became eternally established. That which is the digit of the new moon (amāsoma-kalā) is situated at the door of Brahman.

There, the pure water that had gone and fallen into the heart of Kauṇḍilī became the nectar-like essence of Kauṇḍilī, which issued forth from his body. By merely tasting it, people indeed become free from old age and death.

Free from wrinkles and grey hair, and devoid of all diseases— O Goddess of gods, [these qualities are attained] merely by drinking [the elixir], how much more so when one possesses the mind of mantra! Especially those scents of camphor, agallochum, and musk.
Even one with a divine body, though their soul is satisfied, may become subject to rebirth if the seed [of karma] has not been burnt away.
[They may suffer from] the eighteen types of leprosy, fever, disease, poison and the like,
as well as various terrible poisons and numerous diseases of the eyes.
O Goddess of Gods, by merely drinking it, one becomes a possessor of all siddhis.
First, the worship and adoration of the assembly of Yoginīs is beneficial.

O Goddess, [I praise] the presence of Kulakaula, the Mistress of Yoga (Yogeśī), and Vīravallabha; [I praise] Vīranātha himself, the destroyer of the bonds of worldly existence (bhava-bandha); Bhava, the source of worldly existence (bhavodbhava), the state of being (bhāva), that which is grasped through contemplation (bhāvagrāhya), and the ender of worldly existence (bhavāntaka).

It reduces to ashes everything born of *māyā*, *āṇava*, and *karma*—bestowing the accomplishment of all goals through touching, seeing, eating, or drinking it. Arising from the center, it is to be established in the middle; it is auspicious, bestowing the state of the center.
Born of the family, come from the family, the mother of the family, and beyond both family and non-family—
these are the lineages of the family who abide in the presence of the vessel of the hero.
Those heroes who do not trust [others], yet are benefactors suited to themselves.
When one performs the conduct like a hero while remaining established in the self,
yet the world comes to know of it, then success perishes; for through that [notoriety],
one's lifespan, wealth, vigor, and the power of one's success and intellect are lost.
All the Yoginīs and the mantras born of the Kula carry [the practitioner] away;
one of purified intellect attains the true essence of the instruction on Yoga, the state of moving through the sky (khecaratva),
all effects and causes, and various supernatural accomplishments (siddhis).
For this reason, the origin of the Yoginīs must always be kept secret;
it remains firmly established within the hands of one who has attained [the realization].
Then, that assembly (melāpaka) becomes like the wish-fulfilling gem (cintāmaṇi).
The bringing together of the assembly of the Kula-group and especially of the lineage is declared to be the "manifestation" (saṃnidhīkaraṇa) within the Kula that arises from Ucchuṣma.
For this reason, O auspicious lady, one shall indeed become a possessor of accomplishment through secrecy.
One attains the state of a sky-walker (khecarī) and becomes the sovereign of all worlds;
through the diversity of forms, one becomes the agent of creation and destruction.
By consuming [it] even once, one becomes known as a Candrakāpālika.
And one region at the edge of Śiva, likewise at the place that severs the bonds;
there all sufferings perish, and one becomes a lord of the eight islands.
O Bhairavī, O beautiful one, for the entire assembly of Kulakaula, for the circle of Mothers (mātṛcakra),
and for all the Tantric conduct known as Bhairava,
the substance for invocation has been specifically prescribed along with the mantra.
One should bestow [the practice] with effort when joined with the mantra; without the mantra, it is not accomplished.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
"You have spoken of the Solitary Hero (ekavīra), but the mantra has not been revealed."

I wish to hear that by which she attains accomplishment, by which the substance becomes the essence of the Goddess, by which immortality may be attained, and by which the presence of the heroes may be secured— namely, how the Kula-accomplishment comes to be.

The supreme Kula-siddhi is the most essential, established in the midst of all things. Therefore, O Lord, by your grace, tell me the supreme ritual joined with mantra, which bestows Śiva— the Lord of Mantras, the Leader of Mantras.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen with a one-pointed mind, O blessed lady; I shall tell you that which is not to be told.
That which is named Kuṇḍalinī, whose station is secret and who is eternal.
Resembling white and red in appearance, flowing into the center of the womb,
and situated within the secondary opening of the practitioner's penis—
that mantra of her, the Goddess of the gods beyond the gods, I shall now tell you.
The supreme Kaula is inexpressible; it is the definitive conclusion of the essence of Kula.
O noble lady, by the mere recollection of this, the Yoginīs together with the Mothers, numbering as many as the heroes, manifest their presence.
Known as Saṃsāradamanī, she cuts the bonds of worldly existence; known as Dāridryadamanī, she destroys possession by spirits and epilepsy.
She is celebrated in the Picu Tantras as the beloved of the non-dual way of life.
The supreme *kalā* is the pacifier of the arising of conceptual construction, possessing tranquil vigor;
she is peaceful, born of peace, gentle, and the supreme bestower of bliss and good fortune.
She who pacifies untimely death and devours even the end of time—
Bhairavī, by whose mere remembrance and by whose recitation here,
the supreme powers (parāvibhūti) stand at his disposal within the realm of Śaṅkara.
I shall describe this [state] which is named "Bestower of Sovereignty" (Vibhūtidā) and yet is nameless;
it is known neither by anyone at Karṇa-deśa nor at Prayāga.
O Goddess, it is the Unstruck (Anāhata), the Struck (Āhata), the Mistress of Life, and the Beloved of Life.
O lady of excellent complexion, the third [syllable] is joined with the beginning of *spandana*.
The third is indeed upon the support of the moon (*caṃdrādhāra*), while its own support is the fifth.
Then, O Goddess, it ascends to the abode of fire (*vahniveśma*), not conjoined [with anything else].
The three skull-colored syllables are preceded by one joined with a goad;
the second is likewise joined with a goad, and the third is the leader of the syllables.
O Goddess of the gods, one should join that very [syllable] at the end of the fifth.
The Lord of Mantras, the leader of mantras, joined with the five ending in *homānta*,
is the essence of the Mata, the most excellent doctrine, extending over nine crores [of verses].
From its center, it has emerged like a wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*).
Free from austerity and recitation, devoid of afflictions and exertion,
there is no mantra equal to this one with the water of Śiva;
for by its mere remembrance, the fetters are indeed reduced to ashes.
It is the supreme means for uprooting the suffering of the ocean of existence. Indeed, she is the supreme abode of the wish-fulfilling cow; though free from desire, she is the source of all desires.
Moving according to her own will, she dwells within the very core of the life-force of all beings.
The middle [channel] is situated in the center of the central aperture; it is remembered as the auspicious middle one.
From this alone, and not from anything else whatsoever, arise the origin and dissolution of the entire universe in its particularity.
It is non-conceptual, free from appearance, both pure and impure, and auspicious;
it is the destroyer of conceptualization regarding both auspicious and inauspicious karma. (132b)
But that one supreme [power] has indeed arisen, certain and intent upon restraint.
This digit (kalā) named Amā is truly terrifying and has the mantra as its body.
Therefore, one should protect it with effort; if it is not protected, death will occur.
It must not be given to just anyone, for it would result in the loss of life. To one in whom the ninefold wheel has been described by me as before,
they devour and crush his body.
They sport here according to their desire, just as enemies are [the targets] of enemies.
[Consider] the fat, marrow, grease, semen, blood, flesh, and likewise the skin;
all the skeletal parts and organs of action, which rely upon beauty and youth.
The intellect of the mind, egoism, the collection of the subtle elements and the senses,
truthfulness, purity, longevity, and the meditative cultivation born of mantra-yoga—
all these are forcibly destroyed by one whose face is loud with rage.
For it must be kept secret and is not to be told; by telling it, it becomes revealed.
O Bhairavī, O fortunate one, it arises in this very way without deliberation; for this [teaching] eradicates [all else] in two ways.
One should maintain secret conduct alone and utterly sever [worldly ties];
the deluded soul who reveals [his practice] faces the danger of falling in the second case.
Knowing this, act with diligence toward that which you desire.
This Goddess, the Sovereign of the Gods of gods, is accomplished through a single means:
by meditating upon and reciting [the mantra] in conjunction with the eightfold union of Kuṇḍalinī, she is accomplished.
This, O Mother of the Gaṇas, is the supreme and ultimate means of deliverance for the practitioner here.
Possessing great meritorious karma, he undergoes rebirth for only one more birth;
known as "The Fearless One," he stands at the forefront of all devourers.
Such are the virtues of him in whose heart this latent impression (vāsanā) resides.
That Śiva is the practitioner himself who has directly received the mantra from the mouth of a guru;
for whom there is no deity equal [to him], nor any vidyā or mantra.
She is the one who carries [the world], she who is beyond conventional conduct, the imperishable, and the supreme follower.
She is the bearer of the skull, the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā); everything is established within her.
Whatever mantras, whatever great knowledges, whatever goddesses, and whatever Mothers there are—[all are she].
O Dear One, all those who pervade the entire path are indeed established here;
O Bhairavī, so too are the sixty-four Kulas and the cremation grounds.
Furthermore, there are the sixty-four Oḍḍiyānas, crowded with the upper seats (ūrdhapīṭha) and the rest.
There, all [the deities] present become manifest merely by a single recollection;
there is no doubt in this regarding the Vidyā— it is the truth and not otherwise—
until this mantra is directly obtained from Bhairava himself.
When this has been attained, it should be understood: "Today Bhairavī is pleased with me," for he in whose heart the Goddess of the lords of gods, Kapālī, resides.
She who dwells within the skull, the Mother of Mantras, is the fire-drill of the Kula.

By merely remembering this, all accomplishments (siddhis) arise here for the practitioner, provided his mind is free from impurity; there is no doubt. He casts off his ordinary body and assumes a divine form such as that [of the deity].
Alternatively, the practitioner, the master of mantras, seated upon the supreme throne and situated above all the paths, should always contemplate the form of Bhairava;
remaining there, becoming motionless, and free from the objects of the senses such as sound and the rest.
Having produced the knowledge born of contraction, one should remain forever unestablished [in any state].
There, with the mind, one should utter the supreme and beloved Vidyā;
she is renowned as Anāmikā, the Mistress of the Kula, whose limbs are the ritual actions.
By means of the yoga of simultaneous utterance, having taken the nectar from the end of the twelve [fingers] as far as Śiva, who is beyond the sky, one should sprinkle oneself in the heart. Then,
becoming one whose body is shaken (adhūtatanu) and relying upon the supreme reality, one should remain.
One who is endowed with the cultivation of that state and possesses the nature of consciousness and bliss should perceive Mahālakṣmī,
who resides in the supreme abode and is situated in the sky.
Through the worship procedure of the Ciccakra, there is the contemplation of pure consciousness alone;
by means of a perfectly purified mind, she who is of the nature of space and whose body is space is mounted upon the seven Vyomabhairavas, impelled by the Eye of the Unborn (Ajā).
The Goddess, assuming forms at will according to the desire of the practitioner,
is in ultimate reality the Mistress of Gods, exquisitely gentle and beautiful with nectar. Having become absorbed in her and intent upon her, one should enter into the family of Śiva.
That which was previously described as stainless, unafflicted, the mere reality,
self-cognizable, the primordial power, and *manonmanī*—
one should know this to be *Kula*, the eternal state of *Akula*.
Distinguished by the division of *kula* and *akula*, she abides like fire and heat;
from the supreme will of the Unstruck (*anāhata*), she consists of partless knowledge (*niṣkala-jñāna*).
One should know this as the Wheel (*cakra*), wherein everything is established.
The body of the Goddess, which consists of nectar, is the nature of consciousness, characterized by sentience, appearing as a single, undivided orb that is non-manifest in all directions.
He is Śiva; she is the Supreme Power (Parāśakti); and they are both knowledge and the supreme object of knowledge.
Through the union of the mind and consciousness, the practitioner of mantra should remember the mantra within his heart.
For whosoever attains rest therein for even a moment,
he becomes Bhairava himself and possesses the innate utterance (*sahajoccāra*).
Then, having performed the ritual procedure as before, she performs worship of the Yogeshīs and of Śiva; knowing the mantra, she accomplishes whatever is desired by her mind,
performing and recollecting all that through the Kula-vidyā.
According to the rules of family tradition and with the lineage well-concealed,
one should perform the casting off of the body and so forth through a state free from conventional conduct and by means of the action of the *avadhūta*,
as wept over in the *Dūtī* and *Ārṣa* [Tantras].
In the region called Pūrva, as enjoined by the Kula, there is [the goddess] rich with the fragrance of the eastern island;
she is situated above Śakti and beyond the Supreme, by way of the path beginning with wine.

Having understood the doctrine of Śiva and Śakti through the division of Agni and Soma, from the reverse and the direct order, and by virtue of their inseparable union, one should utter the Transcendental Conduct (nirācāra); Kauleśī resides in the heart.

This supreme mudrā of the Goddess is of the nature of consciousness, composed of the immutable power of *cit*, and expressed through her own accumulated supreme radiance; it is indeed nameless and free from bondage.
By means of the bond of the non-dual form, it is the most excellent nectar known as *kapāla*.

And likewise, one should display the khaṭvāṅga here as a pair. Today, the perfected Kaulika knowledge has been revealed to you; through the yoga of inseparable union, this is the doctrine of Kālikāpālikā.
This is the supreme nectar, pure and unsurpassed, the method for ascending;
it is the essence of the ritual placement (nyāsa) in brief, descended from the Great Śrī Bhairava.
It is joined with the nine navels and so forth, applied to all [sites] such as the seat of mantra (mantrapīṭha).
One should worship the Goddess upon the heads of all [the deities], beginning with Bhairavī.
This very Goddess was previously described in the *Matasāra*, the supreme among scriptures;
she is the most excellent Goddess of Great Fortune, renowned as Mahālakṣmī.

Having performed the sacrifice as previously described, following the sequence beginning with initiation, one should demonstrate the sacrifice according to the rule; that is his commitment (samaya), and not otherwise.
By merely seeing it here, one is liberated from the bondage of worldly existence.
O one of great asceticism, for whom this yoga is equal [to all],
it is the truth that its fruit cannot be described even by hundreds of millions of tongues;
nevertheless, O beautiful goddess, it has been told to you in brief.
The practitioner who knows this thus shall ascend to the great siddhi;
together with his entire retinue, he attains the eternal state.
What else shall I say? For in reality, there is nothing other than this.
"The prosperity of this family of the practitioner has been told to you.
Thus, everything regarding the supreme Kaulika [teaching] has been explained out of affection."

O Goddess, I shall now proclaim for you the oral tradition of the assembly of the nine Yoginīs, the essence of essences, superior even to the highest desire-granting tree. O auspicious lady, I have not revealed this tradition to anyone else.
The transmission known as the "Arising from Mouth-to-Mouth" (mukhakaulodbhava) passes from mouth to mouth;
it bestows accomplishment upon all tantras and awakens the dull-witted.
One who is unaccomplished and lacks heroism shall go [to ruin], whereas the Power (Śakti) becomes truly great.

If a mantra that lacks the proper ritual application is joined with the middle [practice] during recitation, or if it is joined according to the sequence of the *āvalī*, it will be perfected; of this there is no doubt. Those who have fallen away from the tradition of their own lineage (*svakula-āmnāya*), or those who have fallen due to errors in writing—
Those who are devoid of the oral tradition (vaktranāya) are nonetheless perfected within the Mādhava family;
through worship, sacrifice, and recitation, the Goddess herself becomes manifest.
Furthermore, whatever "unbolting" (utkīlana) there may be, she will explain it all.
One should not give [this] to just anyone, except for a disciple who is firm in his vows,
liberated from the grasping at caste, free from all suspicion, devoid of greed, devoted to supreme non-duality, and cultivated in profound secrecy.
One who is renounced, free from hypocrisy, devoid of anger and envy,
equal toward all beings, truthful in speech, a worshiper of the proper sequence, a devotee of the Goddess with a tranquil mind, and one who eats only what is obtained here— such a person [is fit].
He is not moved by that, nor by affection, nor ever by an offense.
Having honored him according to rule with devotion, he should be revealed; never otherwise.
But he who behaves otherwise is devoured by the host of Śākinīs.
Therefore, with every effort, one should carry out the command of Bhairavī;
one should protect it like the life-breath of a living being, or like wealth from thieves.
Thus has this been declared to you in brief, O beautiful one, in this Tantra.
Indeed, this very [teaching] shall be spoken again in brief on the summit of Mount Mandara,
O fortunate one, within the Mahāmādhavaka lineage.
This secret Kālīkula has come down through the succession of oral transmission.
What else shall I say? Speak, O Mistress of the Wheel, O Vandi!
Thus ends the Chapter on the Kālīkula in the fourth Ṣaṭka of the Śrī Jayadrathayāmala, the twenty-four thousand [verse] work.
Having thus heard about the great Kula known as Kālikā, O Goddess of Gods,
she prostrated before the Lord of Gods, who is worshipped by the deities, and spoke again.
The Śrī Devī said:
"I am satisfied, Blessed One, having heard this flood of perfect knowledge.
Now I wish to hear the ritual procedure for the *cakramelāpaka*. How is the Goddess to be propitiated—the Mistress of the Heart, the auspicious Kālikā?"
Having heard these words of the Goddess, which caused the great discus of Indra to tremble,
he who has the crescent moon as his crest-ornament spoke this with a loud laugh.
Śrī Bhairava said:
Excellent, excellent, O illustrious one, vessel for the sake of all knowledge!
O daughter of the mountain,
today I shall explain to you the fierce ritual of the Mistress of the Three Wheels, which brings about the gathering of all.
Having reached the Hero’s Place (vīrasthāna), one should spread out the auspicious Mātṛkā. Having worshipped the Vidyā with all the services due to a hero, one should extract [the mantra]:
the letter ending in *ṣ* (ṣa), the letter ending in *s* (sa), Mahākāla, the Abode (dhāman), and the *āpāsa-binduka*.
O Great Goddess, this *piṇḍa* is the devourer that swallows the three worlds;
it is marked by the abode of the Kevalin, which is devoid of the *kuṇḍala*.
Furthermore, its initial portion, conjoined with the *dhāma-akuśa*, should be extracted again.
Then the *kuṇḍala* and so forth should be given; again, the arm together with the dwelling.
Again, another [should be given] beginning with *sarva*; O Dear One, two more should be placed above it.
One should write the *tribindu* [symbol] following the fifth [letter] situated in *Citrabhānu*.
Furthermore, from the third [syllable], the first should be given; preceded by the womb (yonipūrva), together with fire (savahnika),
and joined with the abode of fire (vahniveśmasamāyukta)— one should extract this "fire" (vadva).
That peak [the syllable *va*] ends with *Varuṇa* (the nasal *m*), and the arm [the syllable *bha*] is marked by two dots (*bindu*).
Having placed *Nāda* and *Vahni* (*ra*) there, then join it with *Sṛṣṭi* (*i*).
Having doubled *Bhīmāṅkuśa* (*ya*), this Vidyā is the most excellent of all.
The eighteen-syllable Ghorā, who devours and consumes the three worlds,
who grants all accomplishments, the fierce one who bestows the siddhi of the *cakramelāpa*,
I meditate upon that Supreme Bhairavī, who resembles a dense, smokeless sky.
Lean-limbed, with a formidable face, possessing a universal form and great majesty,
she is mounted upon a great corpse, with all her weapons raised in her hands.
She is either Parāparā or Śuddhā, or indeed Aparā or Parā.
Thus one should meditate upon the Goddess of gods, who stands behind them;
and those goddesses are stationed upon the stake, seated upon great corpses.
Then the Goddess, whose seat is a human corpse, is most terrible, most fierce, and adorned with hand-bells.
Having meditated thus, one should worship her who stands upon the trident in the center of the maṇḍala with all the offerings for a hero— the solitary heroine who is difficult to approach.
Having worshipped her in this manner according to the rite, [the mantra] emerges from the belly of Kaṃda.
During the Mahāśūla [rite], one should first worship Viśvacaṇḍā and thereafter begin the sādhana.
Having reached the Hero’s Place (vīrasthāna), one should recite the mantra of one hundred thousand syllables;
having offered a *pala* of great hero-flesh as an oblation, one beholds the Supreme Goddess.
Then, O Mother of the Gaṇas, the state of the sky-farer (khecarī) rises upward from that very [place] for the practitioner;
of this there is no doubt—it is the truth, the absolute truth. Or else, one who desires the melaka (union) should perform this rite.
Having gone to the cemetery at night, the practitioner, firm in his resolve,
should go together with many excellent heroes born of all castes;
or this great-minded lord of practitioners may go alone, taking hold of a corpse.
O fortunate goddess, having mounted the back of a goat and bound the hand-bell mudrā,
as many as a hundred times you recite [the mantra], O goddess, so many deities will arrive.
One should offer them the guest-offering (argha) after cleaving the left side of one's own body.
Thereupon, the sky arises together with them, and the practitioner, honored by the gods, becomes like Bhairava himself, O Goddess; of this there is no doubt.

The mantra-practitioner performs subjugation, attraction, inciting enmity, killing, eradication, and so forth with ease; no deliberation need be made in this matter. Indeed, other rites as well have been proclaimed by me previously.
O Goddess of the gods, one should practice these [mantras] until the Supreme Goddess is attained.
She who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation has been described to you according to the truth.
You must keep her strictly secret; she is not to be given to just anyone.
Thus has she who bestows good fortune been described; what else shall I tell you?

Thus ends the chapter on the Sādhana of Parāntakālī in the *Jayadrathayāmala*, the great tantra of twenty-four thousand verses, within the *Śiraścheda* division of the Vidyāpīṭha in the Bhairava-śrotas, in the fourth Ṣaṭka.
The Goddess said:
"O Blessed One, everything has been narrated by you from the beginning in due order.
Now I desire to hear about the supreme arising of great fortune."
By means of which incomparable good fortune arises among practitioners and others;
by which there is belovedness in this world and mastery over all mantras;
O Mahādeva, by which there is auspiciousness and fitness as a vessel for every spiritual accomplishment.
"O Lord of the Gods, tell me that means by which [this] may be produced.
Śrī Bhairava said:
"Listen, O blessed lady, for I shall explain it exactly as I have been requested."
O slender-waisted one, having spread out the Mātṛkā, the goddess who is the essence of all, named *Mahābhāgyodaya*, and having worshipped her according to the ritual rule,
Thereafter, one should extract the Vidyā which bestows happiness, good fortune, and prosperity.
[The first syllable is] the end of Varuṇa (va) joined with Vahni (ra), marked with a Bindu;
likewise, the second leader of the letters is Mahānāda (ha).
One should extract [the mantra] ending with Varuṇa, joined with the Praṇava; then Varuṇa alone, preceded by Kāla and overcome by the Aṅkuśa;
and again Kāla preceded by the Aṅkuśa, marked with three dots (bindus) below the Aṅkuśa.
One should extract Gaṇendra together with Vāyu, preceded by Kāla and pierced by Rudra;
then, in one place, one should extract the House of Fire (the letter Ra) like a goad (the letter U);
thereafter, one should extract Sadāśiva (the letter Ma), Bhīmaśa (the letter La), and the end of the oblation (the letter Ha).
This fourteen-syllable Vidyā is the most supreme of all;
it brings about the arising of great fortune and bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
O Goddess, by the mere recollection of this, even that man who has committed evil deeds [is purified].

Even one born in a family of slaves may hold sovereignty over a kingdom, of this there is no doubt. Indeed, O Beloved, for this very Goddess of Gods, there is no need for a lunar day or for vows and the like; [she is attained] solely by remembering her within the great lotus in the center of the heart.
She bestows great good fortune, grants liberation, and increases worldly enjoyment.
O Goddess, listen now to her worship and likewise to her ritual service. Having reached an auspicious place, one should indeed perform the sacrifice there.
Having drawn the mandala that grants all desires, with a lotus at its center,
one should place therein the goddess Bhāgyakālī, who possesses great power;
she is beautiful, resembling a red lotus, and has a perfectly proportioned body.
Adorned with all ornaments and decorated with necklaces, garlands, and strings of flowers;
likewise, she is seated upon a great lotus and holds a great lotus;
white in complexion, she holds a noose and a goad, and her hand is beautified by a skull-cup.
One should meditate upon her who has three eyes, is endowed with all auspicious marks, and resides within a cluster of lotuses—
she who is the sole heroine, most exalted, and radiant with flashing rays of light. (137a)
One should visualize her raining down a great flood of thousands of jewels;
having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), one should then satisfy her with wealth and various kinds of offerings, such as wine, meat, and spirits.
Then one should perform a fire sacrifice with *bilva* fruits mixed with clarified butter.
Having worshipped a water-pot encircled with a silk cloth, garlands, and perfumes,
and having consecrated it one hundred times with mantras, one should sprinkle oneself with its contents.
Immediately upon being consecrated, he becomes fortunate like another Kāma in person;
he becomes an object of longing for the wives of the lords of the gods.
Endowed with all good fortune and possessed of all supernatural powers (*siddhi*), he flourishes.

For the lord of heroes certainly becomes so through consecration; of this there is no doubt, O Goddess, if he takes refuge on a mountain peak. If the lord of heroes indeed recites [the mantra] five hundred thousand times with his mind absorbed in that meditation, [he attains perfection].
They enjoy the entire earth under a single umbrella immediately upon the conclusion of the recitation.

O Supreme Goddess, the practitioner should perform the fire-oblation (homa) with mantras using bilva, guggulu, and palāśa flowers, as well as lotuses, for the fulfillment of his spiritual attainments (siddhi).
Thus, Kālī is the most supreme of all, the bestower of the fruits of all desires;
she is renowned as Śobhāvatī, the beloved who arises from great fortune.
O Maheśānī, this is your name; what more do you wish to ask?

Thus ends the "Ritual for the Arising of Great Fortune" in the fourth hexad of the *Jayadrathayāmala*, the great tantra of twenty-four thousand verses, within the *Śiraścheda* section of the *Vidyāpīṭha* in the *Bhairavaśrotas*.
The Goddess said:
Now I wish to hear about the supreme destroyer of poison;
O Bhairava, tell me how the highly fortunate Kālī [performs it].
Śrī Bhairava said:
Listen, O you who are saluted by the Lord of the Gods, to this supreme secret,
which pacifies the pride of poison and destroys the evil dreams of the Kali age.

Listen to that peerless ritual of the Goddess, which brings down wicked serpents; she who is the ender of the Kulikas is the supreme sovereign. Having worshipped the Goddess Mātṛkā, one should thereafter extract the Vidyā.

Joined with the Lord of Birds (Kha) and Fire (Ra), marked by the Mohanī (Ū) and the Bindu; again, the Lord who is the Master of Birds (Kha), joined with the abode of Fire (Ra) and the Lord of Gaṇas (La),
ending with Varuṇa (Va), sharpened by that [Fire], and marked by three Bindus— this is Bāhu.
One should extract the letter of withdrawal (ha) joined with the sixth (u), adorned with the bindu and nāda;
then the letter preceded by the womb (ya), situated as the fifth (e), and Śakra (la) marked with three bindus.
Again, one should extract the nectar (sa), preceded by the womb (ya) and marked with three bindus.
Having again bestowed the arm grown from Varuṇa, marked with the three drops and belonging to Varuṇa,
as well as the flood of nectar, he established Gaṇendra in the fire; then, once more,
he gave the pure nectar that prohibits the mark of the three drops.
Soma, who is united with Varuṇa, joined with creation, and possessed of great power—
this nineteen-syllable Vidyā is the destroyer of the Kulika.
Seated upon the shoulders of Tārkṣya, she should be worshipped as adorned with a serpent-girdle.
Well-tanned, resembling a dark blue cloud, and adorned with bells, that Great Goddess has three eyes; with those [eyes], she destroys ten million suns.
Devouring the great serpents of the Kula and drinking the flow of wine, she prevails.
One should worship Karaṅkiṇī according to the prescribed rule with all the ritual offerings, she who is radiant with the sound of a terrible *huṃkāra* and who destroys fear;
one should satisfy her with wine, spirits, and meats.
One should offer the finest meat; then she will be thoroughly accomplished.
From that time forward, O Goddess, she may consume mountains of poison.
What wonder is there that she devours the entire race of the *kulanāgas*?
Wherever one remembers the Goddess, even at a distance of a hundred *yojanas*,
the lords of serpents perish and mountains of poison fall away.
Poison goes to destruction; what is the use of saying more?
Poison is of many kinds: that which is stationary (*sthāvara*), that which is artificial (*kṛtrima*), and likewise that which is called mobile (*jaṅgama*);
furthermore, there is that which is called "doubt" (*śaṅkā*), that which is called "iron-sign" (*lohaliṅga*), and the extremely terrible one called "spider-web" (*lūtā*).
O fortunate one, by the mere sight [of this], the lord of practitioners shall destroy [all obstacles].
By striking [the ground] out of wrath, he shall agitate the realm of the Nāgas.
Having gone to the excellent mountain, O auspicious lady, he should recite [the mantra] according to the number of syllables.
One hundred thousand recitations for the Great Hero, ending with "Salutation to Plava";
endowed with all sovereign powers, he is like a second Bhairava.
Alternatively, by means of one hundred thousand recitations, one may accomplish all rites.
The practitioner shall accomplish subjugation, attraction, inciting enmity, killing, eradication, and so forth;
the foremost among these being the suppression of serpents and the destruction of the ninety-eight [diseases],
as well as other various rites.

Thus has been fully explained to you, O Maheśvarī, the renowned *Nāgāśanī*, which subdues poisons, together with its secret teachings. [End of] the Fourth Ṣaṭka of the *Jayadrathayāmala*, the Great Tantra (*Mahātantra*) consisting of twenty-four thousand verses, within the *Śiraścheda* section of the *Vidyāpīṭha* in the *Bhairavaśrotas*.
The Chapter on the Ritual for the Thunderbolt of the Nāgas.
The Illustrious Goddess said:
Now I wish to hear about the terrifying Meghakālī.
O Supreme Lord, tell me of that [goddess] by whose grace, O God, the wonderful subduing of clouds is accomplished,
as well as all these other rites;
O Blessed One, tell me of her who bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The illustrious Bhairava said:
Listen, O Meghakālī, who are saluted by the lords of heroes, to that which inspires fear.

Hear of her, O illustrious one, who destroys the afflictions of the three worlds; by the mere remembrance of whom the universe trembles, all the mountains shake, and the serpents flee in the ten directions.

Having reached a secluded place, one should worship the Mother of Mantras with all the services due to a hero; thereafter, one should extract the Vidyā. The [mantra] beginning with Bhairava is fourfold, the last being joined with Sṛṣṭi.
The nectar (amṛta) established by Śakra, marked with a bindu and the praṇava;
having extracted the sixth [vowel] and so forth, it is endowed with the fire-seat (vahnyāsana).
The first is marked with the sign of the house (veśmāṅka), and the second is struck by the goad (aṅkuśa).
The third is pervaded by the Praṇava; the fourth is joined with Sṛṣṭi.
All are endowed with the Bindu, while the Nāda alone is indeed absolute.
The pestle is established upon the Svāga and is provided with the abode of Fire.
One should extract the sixth [vowel] (ū) as it is, followed by the first [consonant] (ka) marked with a goad (ankuśa), and then the solitary moon (ca).
Likewise, the wind (ya) should be added, obstructed and restrained by the spike (śa).
This fifteen-syllable Kālī wards off thunderbolts from the clouds.
She is renowned as the bestower of all prosperity, yet Kālī, she who instills fear even in Time itself.
Resembling the sky filled with black clouds and like a great mass of mist,
she is fleshless, deformed, and fierce, striking down ten thousand fires of universal destruction.
Mounted upon a great Tārkṣya, wearing human ears as ear-ornaments,
adorned with a necklace of serpents that brings about the destruction of the royal nāgas,
the Goddess wields all weapons and is the sole devourer who swallows the world.
Having meditated thus, O Goddess, one should place [the deity] upon the lotus in the mandala.
One should worship Karaṅkiṇī with all the offerings for the heroes.
Situated in the midst of the void and endowed with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), she bestows perfect accomplishment.
Having thus worshipped her, that goddess should afterwards perform three hundred thousand recitations;
at the conclusion of the recitation, one should perform the best oblation there, consisting of one-tenth of the number of recitations.
Then, by the power of the Goddess of the Gods, his celestial chariot— which fulfills all desires and is endowed with wish-fulfilling trees— shall approach him as he departs.
Upon hearing this, he shall become manifest as the Lord Bhairava himself.
Alternatively, he shall accomplish the siddhis by means of sacrifice alone—
those common ones which were previously described by me to you within the Tantra.
These are to be employed for the subduing of clouds through the consecration of ashes and mustard seeds with mantras.
Then one should ward off that fierce cloud, which resembles the dissolution at the end of time.
O Goddess, within a hundred yojanas, a boundary is established;
all the lords of serpents, beginning with Ananta, flee in fear.
O fortunate one, if the cloud does not vanish with a single recitation,
then, with an angry mind, one should recite it three times. O Bhairavī, [the cloud] will burst asunder in a hundred ways, even the head of the entire family.

Thus, O beautiful lady, the pacification of clouds has been explained to you. However, the secret known as Ekavīra must not be told to just anyone. Now, what shall I speak further? Tell me, O daughter of the mountain.
Thus, in the Bhairava-stream, in the Vidyāpīṭha, in the Śiraścheda, in the Jayadrathayāmala Mahātantra, in the twenty-four thousand [verse] work, in the fourth Ṣaṭka,
this is the chapter on the ritual of Meghakālī.
The venerable Goddess said:
Now speak, O Lord of Gods, [of that goddess] who crushes all the netherworlds,
who shatters all mechanical devices, who attracts all women,
who agitates the underworld, and who is fierce— [she who is attained] by mere recitation alone.
"O Mahādeva, that indeed is the great and powerful *tamākhyā*, together with its secret.
Śrī Bhairava said:
'Excellent, excellent, O highly fortunate one! I shall explain this question to you.'"
(139b) O Goddess, that which was concealed by me— listen now to it from me:
having reached an auspicious sacred site, one should worship the Mother of Mantras.
Then, by means of the ritual procedure for all heroes, one should extract the Vidyā.
One should first extract it three times, and then extract the Haṃsa.
Kāla, joined with the Praṇava, is at the beginning; then again, that alone.
O Supreme Goddess, one should extract Gaṇendra alone, then again Pañcamādya, and Trisūryaka; between these two, one should extract Varuṇa.
Having extracted Nāda three times, one should take Vahnibīja along with the Bindu.
First, the [syllable] marked by a goad; second, that covered by the deluding [power];
third, that produced from the sixth [vowel], possessing three dots as its watery portion.
One should again extract the first part of the bow, and then the arm alone.

This word is repeatedly practiced; it is immortal, accompanied by the bindu, and pervaded by the *saṃhāra-praṇava*. Then, having extracted the first syllable of *kāla* alone, and subsequently the wind-syllable (*samīraṇa*), divide this word into two parts.
